rubric.why: Distance is the total length of the actual path travelled.
rubric.description: Defines distance as the length of the actual path.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that distance is the total length of the path travelled.

rubric.why: Displacement is the shortest straight-line change from initial to final position, with direction.
rubric.description: Defines displacement and identifies its direction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that displacement is the shortest straight-line change in position and has direction.

modelAnswer: Distance is the total length of the actual path travelled; it is a scalar quantity.
Displacement is the shortest straight-line change from the initial to the final position and has direction; it is a vector quantity.

items.followUp: Define velocity and write its SI unit.

rubric.why: Acceleration describes how quickly velocity changes with time.
rubric.description: Defines acceleration as the rate of change of velocity with time.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct definition.

rubric.why: The SI unit of acceleration is metre per second squared.
rubric.description: Gives the SI unit of acceleration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct SI unit.

modelAnswer: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity with time.
Its SI unit is metre per second squared (m/s²).

items.followUp: State Newton’s first law of motion.

rubric.why: Inertia is the property that resists a change in an object's state of motion.
rubric.description: States that inertia resists a change in state.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that inertia resists change.

rubric.why: The state that an object tends to maintain is rest or uniform motion in a straight line.
rubric.description: Identifies the state of rest or uniform motion that is maintained.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning rest or uniform motion.

modelAnswer: The law of inertia states that an object tends to resist any change in its state of rest or uniform motion in a straight line.
This property of matter is called inertia.

items.followUp: Name two methods used to reduce friction and briefly explain each.

rubric.why: A lubricant forms a layer between surfaces and reduces their rubbing.
rubric.description: Gives lubrication as one way to reduce friction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming lubrication or the use of lubricants.

rubric.why: Ball bearings or rollers replace sliding friction with smaller rolling friction.
rubric.description: Gives ball bearings or rollers as another way to reduce friction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming ball bearings or rollers.

modelAnswer: Friction can be reduced by applying a lubricant, such as oil or grease, between the surfaces.
Friction can also be reduced by using ball bearings or rollers to replace sliding friction with rolling friction.

items.followUp: Define a force and state what is meant by its point of application.

rubric.why: A rigid body is treated as having unchanging shape and size when forces act on it.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that its shape and size do not change under applied forces.

rubric.why: The line of action is the straight line through the point of application in the force's direction.
rubric.description: Defines the line of action of a force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the straight line along the force's direction through its point of application.

modelAnswer: A rigid body is an ideal body whose shape and size do not change when a force is applied.
The line of action of a force is the straight line passing through its point of application in the direction of the force.

items.followUp: Convert 1500 W into horsepower. Take 1 hp = 746 W.

rubric.why: The conversion uses 1 horsepower = 746 watts and divides the given power by 746 W per hp.
rubric.description: Shows the horsepower conversion relation and method.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for using 1 hp = 746 W and the appropriate division.

rubric.why: 1120 W divided by 746 W per hp is approximately 1.50 hp.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct answer with horsepower as the unit.

modelAnswer: Formula: Power in hp = P ÷ (746 W/hp).
Substitution: Power in hp = 1120 W ÷ (746 W/hp).

items.followUp: Define work and state the SI unit of work.

rubric.why: Power is the rate at which work is done.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining power as work done per unit time or the rate of doing work.

rubric.why: One watt is the power when one joule of work is done in one second.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that 1 W = 1 J/s.

modelAnswer: Power is the rate of doing work, or work done per unit time.
The watt (W) is the SI unit of power; one watt is the power when one joule of work is done in one second (1 W = 1 J/s).

items.followUp: A substance has a mass of 6 kg and a volume of 2 m³. Find its density.

rubric.why: Density is defined as mass per unit volume.
The SI unit of density is kilogram per cubic metre.
rubric.description: Gives the SI unit of density.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct SI unit.

modelAnswer: Density is the mass per unit volume of a substance.
Its SI unit is kilogram per cubic metre (kg/m³).
